title: Polymer Physics
description: A chain made of two partners, each end hunting the other, can only grow as long as the scarcer partner lasts. Carothers saw that a single percent too much of one caps the chains at a few hundred units, however far the reaction runs; Kevlar needs both weighed to a part in a thousand. How long the chains are shows in how thick the solution pours: Mark and Houwink's power law, steeper for stiff rods than for loose coils. Adds both to the Polymeriser.

puzzle.goal: Monomers A and B link end to end; r = N_A/N_B ≤ 1 is their ratio and p the fraction of A ends that have reacted. Write the mean chain length X (Carothers).
puzzle.name: Carothers with an imbalance
puzzle.ask: Find X for r = @{r} and p = 0.995.
puzzle.method: Count the molecules before, (N_A + N_B)/2 in units, and after: every bond made joins two into one, leaving N_A(1 + 1/r − 2p)/2.
